description: Decomposes read latency into its causes, top to bottom: the symptom, then SSTables touched per read, then compaction backlog, then the kernel storage layer, then garbage collection.

panels.description: The symptom. Every panel below it is a candidate cause, in order: more SSTables touched, a slower device, or a longer GC pause.
panels.title: Read Latency ${percentile} (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: All four percentiles at once, independent of the Percentile variable, so the shape of the distribution stays visible. A widening gap between p50 and p999 is a tail problem, not a throughput problem.
panels.title: Read Latency Ladder — p50 / p99 / p999 / max (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Coordinator-side read rate. Use it to tell a latency rise caused by more load from one caused by the read path getting slower at constant load.
panels.title: Read Throughput

panels.description: Unavailable, timeout and failure are different stories: unavailable is a replica count problem, timeout is a latency problem.
panels.title: Read Errors by Status
Cause 1 — how many SSTables a read touches

panels.description: The usual cause. If p99 SSTables per read climbs, the read path is doing more work per request before anything about the hardware has changed.
panels.title: SSTables per Read p99 — top 10 tables

panels.description: p50 against max for the busiest tables. A low median with a high max means a minority of partitions are spread over many SSTables.
panels.title: SSTables per Read — p50 vs max, top tables

panels.description: Total SSTables on disk per table. This is the pool the read path selects from.
panels.title: Live SSTable Count — top 10 tables

panels.description: Total includes obsolete SSTables not yet reclaimed. A ratio well above one means compaction has not caught up and reads are selecting from a larger set than the data warrants.
panels.title: Live vs Total Disk Space — top 10 tables
Cause 2 — why the SSTable count rises

panels.description: Pending tasks on the left axis, completions per second on the right. Backlog rising while the completion rate is flat means compaction is saturated, not idle.
panels.title: Compaction Backlog vs Completion Rate

panels.description: Which table the backlog belongs to. One table dominating points at its compaction strategy rather than at the node.
panels.title: Per-Table Compaction Pending — top 10

panels.description: The thread pool that does the work. Pending here and pending compaction tasks should move together.
panels.title: Compaction Executor — active and pending

panels.description: Kernel block layer latency from ebpf_exporter. This is a genuine histogram, so histogram_quantile is correct here. No job filter: the eBPF exporter does not carry the Cassandra job label.
panels.title: Block I/O Latency p99 by Device Operation

panels.description: The median device latency. If p50 is flat while the read p99 above moved, the device is not the cause.
panels.title: Block I/O Latency p50 by Device Operation

panels.description: Completed block I/O operations per second, from the histogram count. More SSTables per read should show up here as more read operations.
panels.title: Block I/O Operation Rate

panels.description: Filesystem-level latency, one series per operation. The exporter names this probe xfs_latency; it measures the VFS entry points for read, write, open and sync. Compare it with the block layer above: a gap between them is time spent in the page cache and filesystem, not on the device.
panels.title: Filesystem Operation Latency p99

panels.description: VFS read and write call rate from the same probe.
panels.title: Filesystem Read Operation Rate

panels.description: Page cache writes and dirty page marks. Reads served from cache never reach the block layer, so a read latency rise with no block I/O rise is often a cache miss shift.
panels.title: Page Cache Activity

panels.description: Stop-the-world pause time as a share of wall clock, plus ZGC concurrent cycle time for reference. db0/db1 run G1 on JDK 11 and report only pauses; db2 runs Generational ZGC on JDK 21 and reports both, so the concurrent series exists only there.
panels.title: GC Time Overhead (% of wall clock)

panels.description: Mean is _sum/_count and is exact. p99 comes from jvm_gc_duration_seconds_bucket, a real histogram, so histogram_quantile is valid; its default buckets are coarse, so read p99 as a bucket boundary.

targets.expr:
sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_count{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name, le) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_bucket{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: GC Duration by Collector — mean and p99

panels.description: Heap used as a share of the heap limit. Used is summed over heap pools; the limit is taken with max, not sum, because Generational ZGC reports the whole-heap limit on both the young and the old pool while G1 reports it only on the old generation.

targets.expr:
100 * sum by (host_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host", jvm_memory_type="heap"})
  / max by (host_name) (jvm_memory_limit_bytes{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host", jvm_memory_type="heap"})

panels.title: Heap Utilization

panels.description: The pool that executes local reads. Pending work here turns coordinator latency into queueing time.
panels.title: Read Stage — active and pending

panels.description: Whether the caches in front of the read path are actually absorbing work. RowCache is disabled by default in Cassandra, so a flat zero for RowCache in every panel of this row is expected and is not a broken panel.
panels.title: Cause 5 — cache effectiveness

panels.description: Hit ratio per cache and node over the dashboard window. Read it as: a key cache ratio that falls while read latency rises means more reads are paying an extra partition-index seek. Computed from the hits and requests counters, NOT from `cassandra_cache_hit_ratio`, for two reasons, both verified on a live cluster: that gauge is published for KeyCache only, because RowCache and CounterCache expose no HitRate value; and it is a lifetime average since node start, so it cannot be re-windowed to the time range you are looking at. RowCache is disabled by default in Cassandra, so a flat zero or an absent RowCache line is expected and is not a broken panel.
panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio by Cache

panels.description: Cache lookups per second, per cache and node. Read it with the hit ratio panel to its left: a ratio is only meaningful where the request rate is non-zero, and a gap in the ratio line matches a zero here. RowCache is disabled by default in Cassandra, so a flat zero for RowCache is expected and is not a broken panel.
panels.title: Cache Request Rate by Cache

panels.description: Bytes currently held by each cache on each node. Read it against the configured capacity: a key cache sitting flat at its limit while the hit ratio falls means the cache is too small for the working set. RowCache is disabled by default in Cassandra, so a flat zero for RowCache is expected and is not a broken panel.
panels.title: Cache Size by Cache

panels.description: Number of entries held in each cache on each node. Read it with the size panel to its left: entries rising while bytes stay flat means the entries got smaller, and the reverse means they got larger. A key cache whose entry count stops growing has reached capacity and is evicting. RowCache is disabled by default in Cassandra, so a flat zero for RowCache is expected and is not a broken panel.
panels.title: Cache Entries by Cache

list.description: Which pre-aggregated latency gauge to read. The gauges are computed per node; they are never summed or averaged across nodes.
list.label: Percentile
list.name: percentile

list.description: Display unit for latency. The metric is emitted in microseconds, so the value is the divisor: milliseconds divides by 1000, microseconds divides by 1.
list.label: Latency unit
list.name: latency_unit

list.description: Database nodes only. Derived from a Cassandra-only metric, so control and app nodes never appear.
list.label: Host
list.name: host
